evidence.claim: Nelnet describes itself as an operating holding company with businesses in consumer lending, loan servicing, payments, and technology-enabled services, many focused on education-sector customers.

Nelnet disclosures identify Loan Servicing and Systems expenses including communications, software, computer services, subscriptions, and collection costs; its Education Technology Services and Payments segment also includes computer services and subscriptions.
Nelnet offers tuition management and payment-plan services that allow students to split tuition payments across a term.

Federal Student Aid approved Maximus to assume Navient's federal student-loan servicing contract, with borrowers retaining payment histories, account data, login information, and automatic-payment arrangements.
evidence.source_title: Navient Student Loan Borrowers: This Company Will Be Your New Federal Student Loan Servicer

evidence.claim: Aidvantage operates under Maximus and services federal student loans by collecting and tracking payments.
evidence.source_title: Aidvantage Customer Service: What It Can Do and How to Contact

evidence.claim: Flywire provides education payment software and secure payment processing for tuition collection across more than 240 countries and 140 currencies.
Flywire's education payment solution supports domestic payments including ACH, card processing, and 529 plan digital disbursements integrated with student information systems.
evidence.source_title: Receive, Process, and Track Education Payments | Flywire

evidence.claim: Flywire previously announced an expanded partnership with Nelnet including deeper platform integration and real-time payment status updates across Nelnet units including FACTS, Unilink, and FirstMark.
evidence.source_title: Flywire Partners with NelNet - Currentcy - Flywire

evidence.claim: Performant Financial announced in 2018 that it had been awarded a Department of Education contract to provide debt collection services on defaulted federal student loans, with a not-to-exceed amount of $400 million including options.
evidence.source_title: Performant Financial Corporation Awarded Student Loan Recovery Contract from the Department of Education

evidence.claim: The CFPB announced in December 2024 that Performant Recovery was banned from servicing or collecting any student-loan debt and ordered to pay a civil penalty.
evidence.source_title: CFPB Takes Action Against Student Loan Debt Collector Performant Recovery for Illegal Fee Generating Scheme That Cost Borrowers Thousands of Dollars

evidence.claim: Fiserv offers public-sector education payment solutions and states that its capabilities include real-time payment processing, retroactive processing of financial transactions, and reconciliation for non-federal loan programs and federal Direct Loan programs.

Navient reached a CFPB settlement under which it was banned from federal student-loan servicing, making it more useful as a regulatory-risk context anchor than as a clean current beneficiary of the federal servicing node.
evidence.source_title: Navient banned from servicing federal student loans in $120M settlement

memory_update.text: NNI is the cleanest reference public company for student-loan servicing plus education payments because its disclosures map directly to Loan Servicing and Systems and Education Technology Services and Payments.
MMS should remain in the underfollowed lane: Aidvantage exposure is hidden inside government-services/BPO rather than education screens.
FLYW is an adjacent education-payment chokepoint candidate rather than a student-loan servicer; verify education vertical materiality before upgrading.
Need a later pass on large-cap payment processors and credit bureaus such as FI and TRU; they have plausible node exposure but may be too diversified for this underfollowed small/mid-cap pass.
Collections and recovery vendors are not automatically beneficiaries; CFPB actions against NAVI and PFMT show that compliance history and regulatory standing are core bottleneck variables.

node: Student-loan servicing, payment systems, borrower communications, and compliance workflows
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around the less obvious infrastructure layer behind student debt and education payments. The strongest public-market mappings are not online universities themselves, but regulated servicers, government contractors, tuition-payment platforms, borrower-payment rails, reconciliation systems, communications workflows, and compliance-heavy collections infrastructure. The underfollowed lane is promising because many candidates screen as government services, fintech, receivables management, or payments rather than education.
